edits.new: If no combination of exact fragments can express the supplied subject at its level of generality, return {"mask": []} rather than a mask for a broader or narrower subject.
edits.old: If no combination of exact fragments can express the supplied subject at its level of generality, return [] rather than a mask for a broader or narrower subject.

edits.new:
The indexed post labels each whitespace-separated word with its position, starting at 1. Punctuation remains attached to its word. Return only a JSON object with a "mask" array of selections in source order, without overlaps.

Use [start, end] to select whole words from the first position through the last, both inclusive. Both positions are integers. Use [n, n] for one whole word.

To select part of a word, use {"word": n, "text": "selected text"}, where n is the word's position. Copy only the selected text exactly from that word; do not insert markers or copy the unselected characters.

For a fragment containing whole words and parts of words, list the whole-word range and each partial-word selection separately. A partially selected word must not also be included in a whole-word range.
edits.old:
The indexed post labels each whitespace-separated word with its position, starting at 1. Punctuation remains attached to its word. Return only a JSON array of objects, one per mask fragment in source order. Each object has integer "start" and "end" fields naming the first and last word positions, both inclusive. These select the whole words and the original text between them.

To select only part of a boundary word, add "start_marked" for the first word or "end_marked" for the last word: copy that word exactly, inserting ⟦ and ⟧ around its selected part. For a fragment within one word, use "start_marked" only. For a fragment spanning multiple words, the first word's selected part must extend to its end, and the last word's selected part must begin at its start. Omit marking fields for whole words.

edits.new:
<subject>The author repairing their daughter's bicycle on Saturday using secondhand parts</subject>
<response>{"mask":[[1,3],[6,9],[11,12],{"word":13,"text":"parts"}]}</response>
edits.old:

<response>[{"start":1,"end":3},{"start":6,"end":9},{"start":11,"end":13,"end_marked":"⟦parts⟧."}]</response>
